title: Lift issue62424 minStartTS oracle to live GC safepoint on authorized testbed

payload.goal: prove the root minStartTS boundary has the expected user-visible cluster effect: GC safepoint/minStartTS is not pinned by a queued DDL session after implicit commit
payload.expected_next_step: design a testbed-safe live observer: create a long or held ADD INDEX after BEGIN, keep a separate active transaction as control if needed, poll GC/minStartTS/safepoint or equivalent metrics, then classify GREEN/RED/INVALID(harness)
payload.stop_rule: if the testbed cannot reliably hold DDL in the queued window or expose a GC/minStartTS observer, record INVALID(harness) and do not infer product behavior

provenance.source: oracle debt from issue62424 after local RED/GREEN validation

name: Live GC safepoint must not be pinned by queued DDL after implicit commit

payload.p_check: The local root-boundary oracle proved ReportMinStartTS must ignore queued DDL sessions with stale CurTxnStartTS.
payload.q_claim: On a live cluster, this should manifest as GC/minStartTS/safepoint progress not being pinned by a long DDL session after DDL implicit commit.

boundary.before: a session begins a transaction, then runs a long CREATE/ALTER INDEX so the DDL job is queued after implicit commit
boundary.fault: the DDL session remains visible to observers with stale transaction state while the DDL is running
boundary.after: cluster-level GC/minStartTS/safepoint observer advances according to real active transactions, not the stale DDL session

side_effects: GC safepoint lag during long DDL
payload.consequence: if the live lift is RED on a current testbed, the user-visible symptom is GC safepoint/minStartTS being held by a DDL statement that no longer owns the old transaction
payload.experiment_need: convert the upstream integration oracle into a testbed-safe SQL/observer schedule and record RED/GREEN/INVALID

provenance.source: derived from issue62424 validated root-boundary oracle

rationale: the live lift still comes from DDL implicit commit leaving stale transaction-visible state
the broad oracle is the cluster-level stale-state claim that remains hypothesis
the live schedule still starts from DDL inside transaction with a GC observer
reuse the implicit-commit then GC/process check schedule, but execute it on the authorized testbed
the live observer must land while DDL is queued/running and stale CurTxnStartTS could still be visible
